data: Overall, I still recommend the game because the gameplay is excellent,
I would still recommend this game at a AAA price
With regular updates and new content, there's always something fresh to look forward to
Highly recommend this game, great play style if you like card games, cool Marvel characters, excellent quick play sessions
UPDATE: The game is still fun
Pay to win game, would not recommend
Every update just feels worse  and worse
I do not recommend it because of the grind
the gameplay itself is really not fun anymore
The constant crashes are also particularly frustrating: the game freezes, closes without warning, or simply fails to load after matches
This game is advertised as "3-Minute games easy to pick up" yet every match I play takes 4+ minutes.

Great card game. Fast paced and with lots of player interaction and decisions. I'm coming from seven years of Hearthstone where I was Legend more times than I can remember, and this game has a better skill ceiling and matches are over in a fraction of the time.

I have a second account on my phone that is in the endgame and I'm playing this one to see what the new player experience is like again since quite a bit has changed from when I started my first account. So far my experience starting over has actually been a ton of fun and I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes digital card games.

Only negative I could say is that Marvel Snap needs a few more game modes -- but those are promised and coming.
It's fun and fast, so I can play a couple games on my lunch break. It also has enough depth to enjoy for a few hours after work.
The monetization in this game is so scummy and predatory that it makes companies like EA, Ubisoft and Activision look like nonprofit charities.
Played for a while, then randomly banned for no reason. Really cute coming from a game with no texting support and only canned emotes.
It's a great game with comic accurate suits and different versions of cards, in which can upgrade to make them look 3-d and even animated. An overall fun game for marvel nerds

Was fun when it came out. But its now just designed to extract as much cash a possible from you with FOMO tactics.
Rewards have been reduced consistently, and cash bundles have eye watering high prices.

No duplication protection in the highlight cache system, you are awarded with 1k collectors tokens (a Series 5 card costs 6k)
Its uncanny how often you hit a duplicate no matter how many cards you are missing, its almost like it is coded that way.
Stopped playing 1 month ago, will not be back

yet another brilliant game, ruined by a horrid progression system, leaving you against players with cards and strategies that simply aren't available to a newer player.
so much lost potential.

The spotlight cache update missed the mark. They announced a paltry improvement to the system (1k tokens if you get a dupe) while remaining silent about anyone who already received the horrible rewards, and leaving every other extremely unpopular parts of the update untouched.
Amazing game, devoted passionate team. It can be expensive but for mostly cosmetics. Could not reccomend higher (I have way way higher playtime but on mobile)
they deliberately matchmake you against opponents that counter you deck on purpose you'll win 1 out of 6 games don't waste your time or money
Don´t play this game. this is the definition of pay to win. series 5 card unbalanced and only gained by 100 bucks pack. prices absurd. and whoever says im wrong. k..7.s

I used to love this game, but that was under the pretense that things would improve over time. They didn't, and that's a shame. I had hoped that with the PC launch, we'd be adding lots of new content to the game that would allow for better longevity. New game modes, new single-player features, and new ways to engage with the community.

Time and time again, they shot my hopes down. It's just a gacha game, guys. Infinite limited-time events to suck up your time and lots of ways to spend money to make your collection prettier.

Do I find this game fun as a F2P guy? Yes, most of the time, when the meta isn't dominated by pay to win basement dwellers with more money than sense. This game has huge monetization issues, where everything is so grossly overpriced that it is clear the people in charge can't even spell the word shame, never mind understand what it means. The code is spaghetti, which is why it crashes all the time, especially mobile where I can't play the game at all anymore. Every time the developers put out a roadmap for the game they either fail to follow through, provide incomplete updates that take months or years to fix, or make changes that are designed to monetize the game even further at the expense of playability.

It is clear that the game is slowly dying, and the developers are trying to cash out before it does rather than fix things, because the enshitification of everything perfectly describes the downward spiral of this game. Go ahead and download it, but don't spend any real life money on it, all of the art you're buying a license to borrow will go away, and not in the distant future.
The games are quick, the curve to get more cards is fair, and it's way more fun than Hearthstone.

When Ben Brode, the creator of this game, was on Hearthstone at Blizzard he blamed the aggressive monetization on Activision-Blizzard. Then they made this game, and its WAY WORSE. Worst monetization EVER. So predatory. So hard to get ANYTHING. You are NOT gonna have all the good cards just by playing for free, much less all the cards u want.
Simple on the surface but has a lot of depth. Cards can be difficult to get your hands on but if you are better you can still win.

Gameplay is fun, artwork is nice. But the game is unplayable if you are not willing to pay2win hard. You have to spend money to keep up with new card releases and ofcourse the new cards are always overpowered. Their greed is killing the game. It can be saved if they make all cards free and only sell cosmetics. Until then, don't bother playing unless you are a masochist or willing to spend alot.

The game starts out balanced. In my first season I was able to climb to above platinum with out even playing that much. When the new season started I quickly climbed up again but then hit a roadblock of players who all had pay to win cards I haven't even seen yet - in some cases they could literally win with 2 or 3 of those cards and beat my entire deck build. I gave it more and more chances but realized pretty quickly that was going to be par for the course from now on, especially when I would get on a winning streak, next thing you know I'm getting almost every match against p2w players and get knocked down the ladder twice as far as I climed. I eventually uninstalled. This game is trash.
this game is pay to play now if you have a low collection level its ok but as soon as u get in to pool 3 its over

lol. i have almost 1000 hrs in this game, i used to play like every day for 2 hrs or more and after all , in the end i still felt "poor" in this game. Every negative comment y are reading is true. If i wanted to throw monay in cards and still have so little in return i would have started playing yugioh TCG jesus.

Gameplay very very good. Like Smash Up but fast zoom zomm

Also the devs are crazy greedy when it comes to pricing of in-game currencies. Alternate art for a single card could run you anywhere from 25 to 50 CAD.
Usually play this on iphone. Fun, easy to learn, can play for free. If you're a Marvel fan, highly recommend. If you like card games or deck builders, give it a shot.

This is the best strategy game I've ever seen that has entire games in under 3-5 minutes. Very fast paced and a large part of the game is reading what your opponent might be doing on their turn. The part of the game that may be annoying for many players however is the immense length of time it takes to collect all the cards.
Easy to learn and understand, but has quite a bit of depth! The only downside is that it's F2P with premium currency and progressing is slow.

Quit Hearthstone and Legends of Runeterra to play this. Haven't had any desire to play anything but Snap since. Might be the card game that packs the most strategy into 5 min games I've ever seen.👍I play 99% on my phone though, played probably a couple hundred hours if I guessed.

I don't recommend playing the game. this game feels like going into a pool that's a little too deep for you as a kid, on the tip of your toes and trying so hard to bounce to the surface for air constantly. never truly at rest or comfort as you are constantly worried about drowning. this game is FOMO weaponized and monetized.

I hate this game.

I hate this game, I hate this game, I hate this game.

And yet I am compelled to play it every day, for near enough a year, because of the addictive tendencies this kind of "free to play" game model preys upon. Tendencies I wasn't even aware I had until I started playing.

Stay the fuck away from this, and anything else that uses this kind of manipulative shit.
Very easy to learn, it's free, and the current player base is mostly dumb, so if you have an IQ of at least 85 you'll win.

Latest update cleared my(and many other peoples progress) i contacted support but they say there is nothing they can do, if i had have bought anything it would be gone now. Also support not only has no steam/pc section so you have to choose either IOS or android and explain in ticket why you arent choosing the correct not available option they also close your ticket if you dont reply within 12 hours making dealing with them an absolute pain.

There is No guarantee that the game wont just wipe your progress on pc in the future so i have to say AVOID THIS GAME.
I'm into anything Marvel Universe. Game play was easy to pick up. The grind isn't too bad and the competition is fun.

"Marvel Snap" emerges as a delightful fusion of the iconic Marvel universe and the addictive gameplay of Snap card games, delivering a dynamic and engaging experience for fans of all ages. From the moment I dove into the game, I found myself immersed in a whirlwind of superhero showdowns, strategic card plays, and thrilling battles.

The game's intuitive mechanics make it easy to pick up and play, yet its depth allows for nuanced strategies and satisfying victories. With a diverse roster of beloved Marvel characters to collect and customize, each with their own unique abilities and traits, "Marvel Snap" offers endless opportunities for creativity and replayability.

Whether I'm assembling the ultimate superhero team or challenging friends in intense multiplayer matches, the game consistently delivers excitement and entertainment, making it a must-play for fans of both Marvel and card games alike.

Really, really fun collectible card game, especially for free to play players. The strategy to the game itself is great, it's like Poker meets Pokemon cards.

*I am not totally F2P: I probably pitch in for $10 monthly "pass" every other month, and I still have the credits and gold I need 90% of the time to do what I want.

First card game I've ever played on PC (Solitaire doesn't count, that shit was peak tho).

So I'm currently making my own card game for Steam and decided to check out the competition. Bro, BIG MISTAKE. Got sucked into this shit like quicksand.

Game is actually GOATED. No PhD required to understand the mechanics, just pure addictive brainrot. Played all damn day like a certified unemployed.

And about the P2W complaints... who tf cares? Why should some basement-dwelling sweatlord with 9000 hours have the most busted deck just because he hasn't touched grass since 2023?

I literally pulled up, bought a couple cards, and started farming people. Skill issue? Probably yours.

Plus, you can unlock tons of cards just by PLAYING. Crazy concept, ik.

The only people crying about monetization are probably 12-year-olds whose moms allow 15 mins of screen time and won't give them lunch money.

Anyway, absolute W game. 10/10.

You can definitely have fun while playing
however
the Micro transactions are very aggressive and overall i wouldnt recommend anyone buy anything inside the game since you can get pretty much everything for free just takes time
Battle pass is a must buy since it has great value and boosts quite nicely the account

Its also a evolving game, a recent game and there is a lot of room to improve
Still one of the freshest card battlers in the scene. Brilliantly designed, well-balanced, and so damn fun. Been playing since day one and still going.

TL:DR :: The game has become too expensive for normal players and has completely killed new f2p users experience.

The reward system has been changed to slow progression. Any large amounts of the currency(s) needed to acquire cards outside of the leveling system have been reduced from the in-game rewards. This has killed any ability for future f2p players from making meaningful progress without monetary investment. Added to that, the rate of new card introduction combined with the cost is just pricing most normal people out.

Examples include: A monthly Season Pass with meta driving cards, Card currency locked in high priced bundles ($75 for 2 cards is crazy), Cards not dropping series (which is supposed to reduce the price of the card over time).

While the core gameplay is quite possibly the best out on the market, the game is, unfortunately, "supported" by a studio that is as inept as their consistent disdain for their own players. Second Dinner has consistently lied to, manipulated, and nickel & dimed the player base to the point where I cannot recommend this game to anyone. If you started out the game today, you would have a ridiculous time trying to catch up in an attempt to acquire enough cards to be remotely competitive. And by then, they'll have released, at minimum, 8-12 new cards, thus further pushing you back down on your journey to collect all the cards.

They constantly say they are working on card acquisition. But at this point, it's clear they're saying it to save face and they do not actually intend on improving card acquisition save for charging you outlandish prices for bundles with the best cards. 

Stay far, far away from this card game.

Very poor community management; "we hear you". Card acquisition is predatory, and feels designed by an algorithm optimized for gaslighting players into juuuust enough abuse to take it. 

Well they messed up; they pushed it a bit too far with the Deadpool's Diner event. 
New players avoid; I feel trapped in a toxic relationship.

I have 192 hours in this! Why? Well guess I must be enjoying it enough. Never paid a penny so err I guess give it a shot. I have no idea. I just look up beginner decks and have unlocked pools 1-3 and game seems fairly generous with events and extra collectors tokens to get more cards.

Will you ever compete with wales and sweats? No but that's ever F2P game. Games only take a few minutes so you have nothing to lose trying it out.

Don't man, this game will suck the living soul out of you. Go, Go away and never come back, brush aside my warning and you are stuck with me here forever
Fun game with no ads. Easy to learn, hard to master. The pay to win aspects are there, but you can easily win without spending money.

One of the best card games I have ever played.
I like it better than Hearthstone because the strongest card is not the credit card.
I like it better than Gwent because the games are much faster and this has a higher level of interactivity.
I like it better than Runeterra because it keeps things much simpler.
I like it better than Artifact because people play this game.

The Snap mechanic is genius. It provides complexity to an otherwise simple game, and rewards players for their skill even when losing.

- There is no catch-up mechanic for new or returning players; you actually can't even buy the cards you'd want to use if you were inclined. If you're new, it will take you MONTHS to amass a collection with cards you see in meta decks.
- Aside from the chore-like build of alliances, they changed the daily log-in reward so that instead of just being once every 24 hours, it was once every 8 hours at a lower rate and would be slightly better than before if you got it every 8 hours.
- The current event running, Deadpool's Diner, is just poker tables disguised as a collectible card game with AGGRESSIVE monetization. Yes, it allows you to refill your "chip pool" for free just by waiting, but even if you could play one table down after a loss, the only way to avoid the pop-up message prompting you to buy more with what amounts to real money is to close the app. With one of the top prizes in the mode being a newly released card, much of the playerbase feels obligated to interact with this mode due to the general cost of card acquisition in the game. This is despite the overwhelmingly negative feedback expressed on the game's Discord server towards the mode. If you like a hyper-competitive ladder environment with more rewards but played out like poker tables, this might be your thing. I despise it.

Excellent characters, great game design, good player competitions!
As a hardcore strategy gamer... This game is Top SS tier game. Not even glazing.
Short gameplay cycle! 10/10.

Battle pass? Nah, more like battle? "pass".

Not about to pay 5 drinks worth of money for some stupid cosmetics. Maybe 2 drinks worth because then at least I can private match with a friend?

Their Gold Pass for 5$ a month looks very promising though! 1800 Gold over 30 day logins.

I have played this game since launch (Collection level 19394), bought every single battlepass, bought several $100 bundles ... and still unable to keep up with a card acquisition. I simply cannot recommend this game to any new players wanting to try SNAP. Its a very fun game and initially getting cards seem ok, but YOU WILL hit a brick wall. On top of that, the developers are one of the worst I have ever experienced; from being completely tone-deaf, terrible customer support, continued lies and lately even taunting the playerbase ... it is time to move on!!!

This game has huge potential but is often squandered due to lack of progression and casual game modes, poor free to play rewards, and ridiculously priced cosmetics. SD has introduced new features that do not seem rewarding enough to justify the grind or have inherent flaws in progression that they refuse to address.

tldr.text: Mixed (68%): players like the gameplay, but the price and monetization draw the most complaints.
Recent reviews are more negative, at 58% positive over the last month, below the all-time score.

details.text: Newer players are far more positive than veterans, at 84% against 53%, and some long-time players say "the gameplay itself is really not fun anymore".
Review bombs, sudden waves of negative reviews, have hit the game more than once, and one month fell to 17% positive, so buyers should check whether a low monthly score is a short flare-up.
